tagline: Once around the North Cascades, with a ferry to close it.
intro: Out of Everett the loop follows the Skykomish River up the western slopes to Stevens Pass at 4,061 feet, comes down into Leavenworth and follows the Wenatchee River into the Wenatchee Valley, long called the Apple Capital of the World. From there it runs north by Lake Chelan to Pateros and up the Methow Valley to the crest of the mountains.

SR 20 brings it down the Skagit to the flood-plain farmland the river built, across Deception Pass to Whidbey Island and south down the island to the ferry at Clinton, which carries it back to Mukilteo. The whole ring is about 440 miles.

moments.title: Leavenworth
moments.text: A struggling logging town remade itself as a Bavarian village from 1965 on, starting with a fire-damaged hotel that reopened as the Edelweiss.

moments.title: Washington Pass
moments.text: At 5,477 feet a 0.2-mile trail leads out to an overlook facing Liberty Bell Mountain, with the highway 700 feet below.

moments.title: Deception Pass
moments.text: Before the bridge of 1935, travelers called the ferry across this channel by banging a saw with a mallet, then sat back to wait.

practical: WSDOT closes SR 20 across the North Cascades, between mileposts 134 and 171, each winter, typically from late November until late April or early May, so the full loop can only be driven from mid-spring through late fall.
